questions.text: A caller claims to be Alice, and the system compares the caller’s voice embedding with Alice’s enrolled reference. Which task is this?

options.A: Speaker identification across the entire enrollment bank.
options.B: Speaker verification against a claimed identity.
options.C: Speaker diarization across the conversation timeline.
options.D: Speech recognition of the caller’s spoken words.

questions.explanation: Verification checks a claimed identity using a 1:1 comparison; identification searches a bank, diarization finds who spoke when, and ASR finds the words.

questions.text: A speaker verifier will serve telephone calls, but its published threshold was evaluated on web-video audio. How should you choose its operating threshold?

options.A: Keep the published threshold because cosine scores are domain-independent.
options.B: Tune it on the final test calls, then report performance on those same calls.
options.C: Use the average similarity among enrollment recordings as the threshold.
options.D: Tune it on held-out target-domain development trials with genuine and impostor pairs.

questions.explanation: Channel mismatch changes score distributions. Choose the operating threshold using representative held-out development trials, and keep the final test set separate.

questions.text: The verifier returns cosine(enroll, test) >= threshold, and cosine returns 0.0 if either vector has zero norm. What does verify([0, 0], [1, 0], threshold=0.0) return?

options.B: False, because zero vectors are explicitly rejected.
options.D: None, because the embedding has no direction.

questions.explanation: The cosine helper returns 0.0 for a zero-norm vector; the inclusive threshold comparison then returns True. The toy verifier has no separate invalid-embedding rejection.
